source_text: 1. QuonramM autem non solum prophetze et justi multi, preescientes per Spiritum sanctum adventum ejus, orayerunt in illud tempus venire, in quo facie ad faciem viderent Dominum suum, et sermones audirent ejus, Dominus fecit manifestum, dicens discipulis: Multi prophet et justi cupierunt videre que videtis, et non viderunt, et audire que auditis, et non audierunt. Quemadmodum igitur concupierunt et audire, et videre, nisi preescissent futurum ejus adventum? Quomodo autem prescire potuerunt, nisi ab ipso preescientiam ante accepissent? Quomodo autem Scripture testificantur de eo, nisi ab uno et eodem Deo omnia semper per Verbum revelata et ostensa fuissent credentibus ; aliquando quidem colloquente eo cum suo plasmate, aliquando autem dante legem, aliquando vero exprobrante, aliquando vero exhortante, ac deinceps liberante servum, et adoptante in filium, et apto tempore incorruptele heereditatem prestante, ad perfectionem hominis? enim eum in augmentum et incrementum, quemadmodum et Scriptura dicit: Crescite et multiplicamini. 2. Et hoe Deus ab homine differt, quoniam Deus quidem facit, homo autem fit: et quidem qui facit, semper idem est: quod autem fit, et initium, et medietatem, et adjectionem, et augmentum accipere debet. Et Deus quidem bene facit, bene autem homini. Et Deus°quidem perfectus in omnibus, ipse sibi eequalis et similis; totus cum sit lumen, et totus mens, et totus substantia, et fons omnium bonorum: homo vero profectum percipiens et augmentum ad Deum. Quemadmodum enim Deus semper idem est; sic et homo in Deo inventus, semper proficiet Deum. Neque enim Deus cessat aliquando in benefaciendo, et locupletando hominem: neque homo cessat beneficium accipere, et ditari a Deo. Exceptorium enim bonitatis, et organum clarificationis ejus, homo gratus ei qui se fecit: et iterum exceptorium justi judicii ejus homo ingratus, et spernens plasmatorem, et non Verbo ejus: qui plurimum semper fructificantibus, et plus habentibus dominicum argentum, daturum se pollicitus est. Euge, inquit, serve bone, et fidelis, quia in modico fidelis fuisti, super multa te constituam; intra in gaudium Domini tui: ipse Dominus plurimum promittens. 98. Sieut ergo nune fructificantibus, plurimum daturum se pollicitus est, secundum munerationem gratize suze, sed non secundum commutationem agnitionis; ipse enim Dominus perseverat, et idem Pater revelatur; sic ergo et posterioribus majorem quam que fuit in veteri Testamento munerationem gratiz attriunus et idem Dominus per suum adyentum. Et illi enim per famulos audiebant venturum regem, et mediocriter gaudebant, secundum quod sperabant venturum eum: qui autem preesentem viderunt, et libertatem adepti et potiti sunt ejus muneratione, majorem gratiam et abundantiorem exultationem habent, gaude regis adventu, quemadmodum et David dicit: Anima mea exultabit in Domino, jucundabitur in salutari ejus. Et propter hoc Hierosolymam introéunte eo, omnes qui erant in via David, in dolore anime cognoverunt suum regem, et substraverunt ei vestimenta, et ramis viridibus adornaverunt viam, cum magna leetitia et exultatione clamantes: Osanna filio David, Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, Osanna in excelsis, Zelantibus autem malis dispensatoribus, qui circumyeniebant inferiores, et eorum quibus ratio non constabat, et propter hoe nolentibus venisse regem, et dicentibus ei, Audis quid isti dicunt? ait Dominus: Nunquam legistis, Ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem? id quod a David in Filium Dei dietum érat, in se factum ostendens, et significans, illos quidem virtutem Scripture, et dispositionem Dei; se autem esse qui a prophetis annuntiatus sit Christus, cujus nomen in omni terra laudatur, ex ore infantium et lactentium laudem perficientis suo Patri: quapropter et elevata est magnificentia ejus super Si ergo idem ipse adest, qui preedicatus est a prophetis, Dominus noster Jesus Christus, et adventus ejus pleniorem gratiam et majorem munerationem attribuit his qui susceperunt eum, manifestum, quoniam et Pater idem ipse est, qui a prophetis annuntiatus est, et non alterius Patris agnitionem fecit veniens Filius, sed ejusdem qui ab initio preedicatus est; a quo et libertatem detulit his qui legitime, et prono animo, et’ toto corde deserviunt ei: contemtoribus autem, et non subjectis Deo, sed in gloriam hominum exteriores munditias sectantibus, (quee in figuram futurorum traditz erant, velut ®umbree cujusdam descriptionem Lege, atque deliniante de temporalibus zeterna, de terrenis ceelestia), fingentibus plusquam quz dicta sunt sese observare, tanquam diligentiam suam etiam ipsi Deo preeferentibus, intus autem plenis hypocrisi, et cupiditate, et omni malitia, sempiternam attulit perditionem, abscindens eos a vita.
pass_a_gloss: For however many prophets and just men, knowing through the Holy Spirit His coming, prayed in that time to come, in which face to face they might see their Lord, and hear His words, the Lord made manifest, saying to the disciples: Many a prophet and just men desired to see what you see, and did not see, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear. How therefore did they desire to hear and see, unless they knew His coming would be? How however could they know, unless they received knowledge beforehand from Him? How however do the Scriptures testify about Him, unless all things were always revealed and shown to believers through the Word by one and the same God; sometimes speaking with His creature, sometimes giving the law, sometimes rebuking, sometimes exhorting, and then liberating the servant, and adopting as a son, and at the suitable time granting an incorruptible inheritance, for the perfection of man? For He says to him for increase and growth, just as the Scripture says: Grow and multiply. And this God differs from man, because God indeed does, but man is done: and indeed He who does is always the same: but what is done, and beginning, and middle, and addition, and increase must be received. And God indeed does good, but good to man. And God is perfect in all things, He Himself equal and similar to Himself; all light, and all mind, and all substance, and fountain of all good things: but man receiving progress and increase towards God. For just as God is always the same, so also man found in God will always make progress towards God. For neither does God cease at any time to do good and enrich man: nor does man cease to receive benefit and be enriched by God. For the receptacle of His goodness, and the instrument of His clarification, man is grateful to Him who made him: and again the receptacle of His just judgment, man ungrateful and despising the Creator, and not obedient to His Word: who promised to give Himself to those always bearing much fruit, and having more, the Lord's money. Well done, He says, good and faithful servant, because you were faithful in a little, I will set you over much; enter into the joy of your Lord: the Lord Himself promising much. Just as therefore now to those bearing fruit, He promised to give much, according to the gift of His grace, but not according to a change of knowledge; for the Lord Himself perseveres, and the same Father is revealed; so also to those later, a greater gift of grace than what was in the Old Testament, the same Lord through His coming. And those indeed through servants heard the King was coming, and they rejoiced moderately, according to what they hoped He would come: but those who saw Him present, and obtained liberty and possessed His gift, have greater grace and more abundant exultation, rejoicing at the King's coming, just as David says: My soul will exult in the Lord, will be joyful in His Savior. And on account of this, when He entered Jerusalem, all who were on the way of David, in sorrow of soul recognized their King, and spread garments under Him, and adorned the way with green branches, crying out with great joy and exultation: Hosanna to the Son of David, Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord, Hosanna in the highest. But to the evil dispensers, who were going around the lower ones, and those whose reason was not constant, and on account of this not willing that the King should come, and saying to Him, Do You hear what these say? the Lord says: Have you never read, You perfected praise from the mouth of infants and sucklings? which was said by David about the Son of God, showing that it was done in Himself, and signifying that they indeed have the power of Scripture, and the disposition of God; but He is the Christ announced by the prophets, whose name is praised in all the earth, perfecting praise from the mouth of infants and sucklings to His Father: therefore His magnificence was also elevated above. If therefore He Himself is present, who was predicted by the prophets, our Lord Jesus Christ, and His coming attributes a fuller grace and greater gift to those who received Him, it is manifest that the Father is also the same, who was announced by the prophets, and the Son did not make known a different Father, but the same one who was predicted from the beginning; from whom He also brought liberty to those who serve Him lawfully, and with a prone soul, and with the whole heart: but to those despising and not subject to God, but pursuing external purities for the glory of men, (which were handed down as a figure of future things, as a kind of shadow and description of the Law, and outlining eternal things from temporal ones, and heavenly things from earthly ones), feigning to observe more than what was said, as if they were preferring their diligence even to God, but inwardly full of hypocrisy, and desire, and all malice, He brought eternal perdition, cutting them off from life.

bible_refs.note: Many a prophet and just men desired to see what you see
You perfected praise from the mouth of infants and sucklings

pass_b_english: Many prophets and righteous men, knowing through the Holy Spirit that He would come, prayed to live in the time when they might see their Lord face to face and hear His words. In response, the Lord made this plain to His disciples: "Many prophets and righteous men desired to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it" (Matt. 13:17). How could they have longed to see and hear unless they had foreknown His coming? And how could they have foreknown it unless they had received that foreknowledge from Him? How could the Scriptures testify about Him unless all things had always been revealed and shown to believers through the Word by one and the same God? At one time He spoke with His creature; at another He gave the law; at another He rebuked; at another He exhorted; and then He freed the servant, adopted him as a son, and at the appointed time granted an incorruptible inheritance for man's perfection. For He says this to him for increase and growth, just as Scripture says: "Grow and multiply" (Gen. 1:28).

This is how God differs from man: God acts, but man is acted upon. The One who acts is always the same; but what is acted upon — having beginning, middle, addition, and increase — must receive these things. God does good, and He does good to man. God is perfect in all things, equal and like to Himself; He is wholly light, wholly mind, wholly substance, the fountain of all good things. But man, receiving progress and increase, moves toward God. Just as God is always the same, so also man, found in God, will always advance toward God. For God never ceases to do good and enrich man, and man never ceases to receive benefit and be enriched by God. As the receptacle of His goodness and the instrument of His manifestation, man is grateful to the One who made him; but as the receptacle of His just judgment, man — ungrateful and despising his Maker, disobedient to His Word — receives judgment. To those always bearing much fruit, having more of the Lord's money, He promised to give Himself. "Well done, good and faithful servant," He says; "because you were faithful in a little, I will set you over much; enter into the joy of your Lord" — the Lord Himself promising much.

Just as He now promises to give much to those bearing fruit, according to the gift of His grace and not according to a change of knowledge — for the Lord endures, and the same Father is revealed — so also to those who came later, the same Lord through His coming attributed a greater gift of grace than what was in the Old Testament. The former people heard through servants that the King was coming, and they rejoiced moderately, according to what they hoped; but those who saw Him present, who obtained liberty and possessed His gift, have greater grace and more abundant exultation, rejoicing at the King's coming, just as David says: "My soul will exult in the Lord; it will rejoice in His salvation" (Psalm 35:9 LXX). And for this reason, when He entered Jerusalem, all who were on the road — the people of David — in the sorrow of their souls recognized their King, spread their garments under Him, adorned the way with green branches, and cried out with great joy and exultation: "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!" But the evil stewards, who went about among the lesser ones and those whose reason was not settled — and therefore did not want the King to come — said to Him, "Do You hear what these are saying?" The Lord answered, "Have you never read, 'Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babies You have perfected praise'?" (Ps. 8:2). This was spoken by David concerning the Son of God, showing it was fulfilled in Himself, and signifying that they indeed possess the power of Scripture and the disposition of God; but He is the Christ announced by the prophets, whose name is praised in all the earth, perfecting praise from the mouth of infants and nursing babies to His Father. Therefore His magnificence was also exalted on high.

If, then, He Himself is present — the One predicted by the prophets, our Lord Jesus Christ — and His coming attributes a fuller grace and greater gift to those who received Him, it is manifest that the Father is also the same One announced by the prophets. The Son did not make known a different Father, but the same One who was proclaimed from the beginning. From Him He brought liberty to those who serve Him lawfully, with a willing soul and whole heart. But to those who despise Him and are not subject to God, who pursue external purities for the glory of men — which were handed down as figures of future things, as a kind of shadow and outline of the Law, sketching eternal things from temporal ones and heavenly things from earthly ones — feigning to observe more than what was commanded, as if they preferred their own diligence even to God, while inwardly full of hypocrisy, lust, and all malice — He brought eternal perdition, cutting them off from life.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause rendering, and Pass B provides a polished English version that maintains the theological nuances (e.g., 'God acts, but man is acted upon' for 'Deus quidem facit, homo autem fit'). Scripture citations in Pass B (Matt 13:17, Gen 1:28, Ps 35:9, Ps 8:2) correctly identify the quoted or alluded-to passages in the Latin. The title 'Desire to See the Lord' captures the central theme of the first paragraph.
